newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland honours ethnic Germans killed by Gestapo.
newsitem.headline: Poland honours ethnic Germans killed by Gestapo.

text.p: Poland on Thursday honoured two ethnic German industrialists who were shot by the Gestapo after they refused to collaborate with Nazi invaders at the start of World War Two, PAP news agency said.
A bronze plaque to Robert Franz Geyer and Gwido Wolfgang John was unveiled on the wall of a textile factory once owned by Geyer in the central Polish industrial city of Lodz.

Both men's families had lived for generations in Poland and when Nazi German forces invaded the country in September 1939 they refused to sign papers showing they were part of dictator Adolf Hitler's idea of the greater German nation.
They also formed a committee to help Polish prisoners held by the Nazis. Gestapo security police shot them both at Geyer's villa in December 1939, PAP said.
The unveiling ceremony was attended by representatives of the German embassy, local authorities and the head of Poland's committee investigating crimes against the Polish nation.
